questions.question: Vikas gave 3 examinations. The respective ratio of marks scored by him in the 3 examinations is 3 : 5 : 6. The respective ratio of maximum marks of the 3 examinations is 5 : 7 : 8. If he scored 50 percent marks in total, then in how many examinations has he scored more than 50 percent marks?
questions.questionHtml: Vikas gave 3 examinations. The respective ratio of marks scored by him in the 3 examinations is 3 : 5 : 6. The respective ratio of maximum marks of the 3 examinations is 5 : 7 : 8. If he scored 50 percent marks in total, then in how many examinations has he scored more than 50 percent marks?
questions.solution:
Given:

So,
14x = 10 ⇒ x = 5/7

Now marks scored in each exam:
→ Exam 1 = 3x = 15/7
→ Exam 2 = 5x = 25/7
→ Exam 3 = 6x = 30/7

Maximum marks:
→ Exam 1 = 5
→ Exam 2 = 7
→ Exam 3 = 8

Percentage = (Marks Scored / Maximum Marks) × 100

→ Exam 1 = (15/7) ÷ 5 = 3/7 = 42.8%
→ Exam 2 = (25/7) ÷ 7 = 25/49 = 51%
→ Exam 3 = (30/7) ÷ 8 = 30/56 = 53.6%

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B can do it in 40 days. B works alone for 2 days and A works alone on the 3rd day. This process continues till the work is completed. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B can do it in 40 days. B works alone for 2 days and A works alone on the 3rd day. This process continues till the work is completed. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
A can do the work in 12 days
B can do the work in 40 days

Total Work = 120 units

A’s 1 day work = 120 ÷ 12 = 10 units/day
B’s 1 day work = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day

👉 B works alone for 2 days,
👉 A works alone on the 3rd day

So, in one full 3-day cycle:
B’s work in 2 days = 2 × 3 = 6 units
A’s work in 1 day = 10 units
Total in 3 days = 6 + 10 = 16 units

Work done per cycle = 16 units
So, number of complete cycles = 120 ÷ 16 = 7 complete cycles (112 units)
Work left = 120 − 112 = 8 units

Next cycle starts again with B (2 days) →
B’s 2 days work = 2 × 3 = 6 units
Work left = 8 − 6 = 2 units

Now A will work next day, efficiency = 10 units/day
So, time taken by A to complete remaining 2 units = 2 ÷ 10 = 0.2 day

Total Time = 21 days + 2 days + 0.2 day = 23.2 days

questions.question: Lakshmi starts from point A at 8:00 a.m. and reaches point B at 2:00 p.m. on the same day. Prem starts from point B at 8:00 a.m. and reaches point A at 6:00 p.m. Both points A and B are separated by only one straight line track. When do they both meet?
questions.questionHtml: Lakshmi starts from point A at 8:00 a.m. and reaches point B at 2:00 p.m. on the same day. Prem starts from point B at 8:00 a.m. and reaches point A at 6:00 p.m. Both points A and B are separated by only one straight line track. When do they both meet?
questions.solution:
Given:

Take LCM of 6 and 10 = 30 km (Assume total distance = 30 units)

Now,
Ram’s speed = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 units/hr
Raju’s speed = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units/hr

They start at the same time (8:00 a.m.) from opposite ends

They are moving towards each other.

Relative speed = 5 + 3 = 8 units/hr

Time to meet

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed
= 30 ÷ 8 = 3.75 hours

3.75 hours = 3 hours 45 minutes

Meeting Time

8:00 a.m. + 3 hours 45 minutes = 11:45 a.m.
